turns.prompt_text: How can I access my google gmail, so that I can have a program listening to incoming in a pub/sub style, or does gmail have an api/setup?
turns.response_html:
Yes, Gmail has a native, built-in solution for exactly this. You don't need to poll the server constantly. You can use the Gmail API integrated with Google Cloud Pub/Sub to push real-time notifications to your program whenever a new email arrives.

Here is exactly how the architecture works: Gmail monitors the inbox. When an email arrives, Gmail publishes an alert to a Cloud Pub/Sub topic. Pub/Sub then immediately "pushes" that alert to your application via an HTTP POST request (a webhook).

Here is how to set up the pipeline.

The historyId Catch

You might notice the payload above doesn't contain the actual email body, subject, or sender. Gmail's push notifications are lightweight—they only tell you that something changed, and give you a historyId as a pointer.

To get the actual email, your application needs to take that historyId and do two things:

  1. Call the Gmail API users.history.list endpoint using the historyId to see exactly what changed (e.g., which specific message IDs were added).
  2. Call the users.messages.get endpoint with those specific message IDs to download the email body, headers, and attachments.
